name: jev-planner
description: One Jev step over a real Chrome page, in both flavours. `step` lets the page-side policy roam (wait for the tab to settle, observe it, return the {operation, element/selector, goal_probability, stuck_probability} decision a chrome_cdp agent_step node executes); `find` resolves a directed *intent* (role/label/href/selector) against the laya-browser extension's numbered snapshot, validates that the element is really clickable, and returns the same decision shape; `observe` draws the numbered overlay and returns a bounded numbered table; `dismiss` closes a full-viewport modal that would swallow clicks. All page logic lives in page/*.js, so the Rust engine keeps the CDP transport, policy and tab lifecycle.
